Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government data exchange systems. 25 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019 provides framework for e-government and electronic communications. However, it is only partially enacted (as of 2025). Draft Data Protection Bill and Civil Registration and Identification Bill are still pending. No specific data sharing/interoperability law exists yet.
revision_notes: Original sources (Electronic Transactions Act 4/2019, LAC PDF and NamibLII text) fetched and confirmed accurate: the Act is only partially in force (Chapters 4-5 and section 20 uncommenced), and while section 14 gives the Minister guideline-making power on government system interoperability, the Act does not itself establish a dedicated legal mandate for cross-government data sharing. Fresh checks (Jan-Feb 2026) confirm no enabling data-exchange legislation is yet in force: the Data Protection Bill remains unenacted, described as merely 'ready to be re-submitted to cabinet' as of 28 Jan 2026 (Channel Africa); the Civil Registration and Identification Act 13 of 2024 was assented to in December 2024 but per NamibLII 'has not yet come into force' as of February 2026. The Nam-X (X-Road-based) government interoperability platform operates under an administrative Interoperability Framework for the Public Service rather than primary legislation. Score of 2 (Under development) confirmed unchanged; comments updated to reflect the Civil Registration and Identification Bill's enactment-but-non-commencement status.
revised_comments: Namibia's Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019 provides a general e-government and electronic-communications framework, including ministerial power under section 14 to issue guidelines on system interoperability, but the Act is only partially in force (Chapters 4 and 5 and section 20 remain uncommenced) and does not itself establish a dedicated legal mandate for cross-government data sharing. The Civil Registration and Identification Act 13 of 2024 has been assented to but has not yet commenced. A Data Protection Bill remains in draft, awaiting re-submission to Cabinet as of January 2026. Government data exchange (the Nam-X/X-Road platform) currently operates under an administrative Interoperability Framework for the Public Service rather than under primary legislation. No dedicated data-sharing or interoperability act is yet in force.
